title.narrative: Envelope 2: (Increase the resilience of IDPs living in camps at Idleb-Harim-Qourqeena and Dana subdistrict by providing free bread distribution to improve lifesaving and life-sustaining food assistance)

description.narrative: This project aims to improve the food security status of the most vulnerable IDP households living in camps in the Harim-Quorqeena and Dana sub-district within the Idleb governorate through life-saving and life-sustaining food assistance by providing free bread which was confirmed by the RNA done recently, where bread is the first priority for 91%. 300 tons of flour will be purchased from Turkey or the local market in (Syria) with the following specifications: the wheat seeds milled from fully mature wheat grains free of filth and rodents excreta clean and free from any foreign material and substances hazardous to health free from rancidity and unacceptable odor or taste homogenous in color and free from agglomeration and suitable for Syrian Bread making number 650. Sent to the bakery to be baked to distribute 574,500 bread bundles (600 g bundle weight) to 2527 HH (14814 individuals) in 16 camps in Harem-Qourqeena and Dana with 5054 bread bundles on daily basis 26 days monthly up to 4 months, from the end of February 2023 to the end of June 2023 by well trained ICO distribution team with great and proven track record dealing with BNFs using a well-controlled mechanism to ensure accountability and transparency. The distribution criteria will be: HH with 1-3 individuals will receive one bread bundle HH with 4-6 individuals will receive two bread bundles HH with 7-9 individuals will receive three bread bundles HH with 10 individuals and more will receive four bread bundles Each ton of flour can produce 1915 bread bundles, the weight of each bread bundle is 600 gram The targeted beneficiaries will be IDPs in 16 camps within two communities in the Harem-Qourqeena subdistrict (SY 070304), and one community in the Dana subdistrict (SY070301): 1-Boz Ghaz, 1 camp (35 HHs, 130 individuals) 2-Kafr Aruq, 14 camps (2412 HHs, 14,084 individuals) 3-Kafr Deryan, 1 camp (80 HHs, 600 individuals) The bread bundle will be distributed for free. The baking cost will be including baking, storing the flour, and transporting the bread bundles to distribution centers in the camps. Bakery Responsibility: 1- Securing a warehouse for flour that will be delivered by the flour supplier. 2- Securing workers to load the flour into the oven. 3- Providing all the necessary materials for bread, such as qua'ity yeast, salt, and bags printed with the human and workers logos, and so on. 4- Delivery of 1915 bundles weighing 600 grams per ton wrapped in a printed bag with the INSAN Logo. 5- Transporting the bread from the bakery to the distribution centers in Harim-Quorqeena camps. INSAN Organization Responsibility: Purchasing flour and delivering it to the bakery warehouse. The procurement process will be in line with INSAN procurement policy by tendering process publicly. Technical specifications of the flour will be appropriate to produce Syrian bread. Production of the bread will be contracted with one bakery and the cost will cover the storing of the flour and the transportation of bread from the bakeries to the distribution points. The project will be the only project distributing free bread (project duration 11th of January 2023 to the 10th of July 2023) and provide 574500 free bread bundles to 16 camps for up to 4 months using distribution blanket modality. All activities will be explained to stakeholders and get feedback along with internal monitoring from the MEAL department. The implementation of all activities will be gender-sensitive, with feeds back from BNFs through different mechanisms suited for illiterates. INSAN team will hand over bread to the tents if the HH is headed by the disabled,
